metadata.description: Core Indian legal corpus for BM25 and ChromaDB retrieval

entries.text: BNS Section 101 (replaces IPC 302) — Murder: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine. The Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) principle applies: death penalty only in rarest of rare cases.

BNS Section 316 (replaces IPC 420) — Cheating: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy any document shall be punished with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

BNS Section 85 (replaces IPC 498A) — Cruelty by husband or relatives: Whoever, being the husband or a relative of a husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine. Cruelty includes harassment for dowry.

BNS Section 152 (replaces IPC 124A sedition) — Acts endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India: Whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication, excites or attempts to excite secession or armed rebellion shall be punished with imprisonment for life or 7 years and fine.

BNS Section 111 — Organised Crime: New provision. Whoever commits organised crime including kidnapping, extortion, contract killing, land grabbing, financial scams, cyber crimes on behalf of a gang shall be punished with death or life imprisonment.

Article 21 — Right to Life and Personal Liberty: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Expanded in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) to include right to live with dignity, right to livelihood, right to health, right to education, and right to speedy trial.

Article 14 — Right to Equality: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. This prohibits arbitrary action by the State and requires intelligible differentia with rational nexus to the objective.

Article 19(1)(a) — Freedom of Speech and Expression: All citizens shall have the right to freedom of speech and expression. Subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2) including sovereignty, integrity, security of India, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency, morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to offence.

Article 22 — Rights on Arrest: No person arrested shall be detained without being informed of the grounds. Right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner. Must be produced before nearest magistrate within 24 hours. Preventive detention provisions under clauses 4-7.

Article 226 — Power of High Courts to issue writs: Every High Court shall have power to issue to any person or authority orders or writs including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari for enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

Consumer Protection Act 2019 Section 35 — Filing of Complaint: A complaint may be filed by a consumer, voluntary consumer association, State or Central Government, one or more consumers on behalf of others with common interest. Complaint filed before District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission for claims up to Rs 1 crore.

Consumer Protection Act 2019 Section 47 — Jurisdiction of State Commission: State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has jurisdiction over complaints where value of goods/services and compensation claimed exceeds Rs 1 crore but does not exceed Rs 10 crore.

Consumer Protection Act 2019 Section 58 — Jurisdiction of National Commission: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has jurisdiction over complaints where value exceeds Rs 10 crore, appeals from State Commissions, and matters of national importance.

Consumer Protection Act 2019 Section 69 — Limitation Period: No complaint shall be admitted by the Commission unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen. Commission may condone delay if sufficient cause is shown.

Hindu Marriage Act Section 13 — Divorce: Either party may petition for dissolution of marriage on grounds of: adultery, cruelty, desertion for 2+ years, conversion to another religion, unsound mind/mental disorder, leprosy (communicable), venereal disease, renunciation of world, not heard of being alive for 7 years.

Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act 2005 Section 6 — Devolution of interest in coparcenary property: Daughter shall be a coparcener by birth in her own right and shall have same rights and liabilities as a son. Supreme Court in Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) held this applies even if father died before 2005 amendment.

IT Act Section 66 — Computer related offences: If any person, dishonestly or fraudulently, does any act referred to in section 43 (unauthorized access, damage to computer), he shall be punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years or with fine up to Rs 5 lakh, or with both.

IT Act Section 66D — Punishment for cheating by personation using computer resource: Whoever by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to Rs 1 lakh.

IT Act Section 43A — Compensation for failure to protect data: Where a body corporate, possessing, dealing or handling any sensitive personal data or information in a computer resource which it owns, controls or operates, is negligent in implementing and maintaining reasonable security practices causing wrongful loss to any person, it shall be liable to pay damages.

RERA Section 11 — Obligations of promoter: Promoter shall not advertise, market, sell any apartment/plot/building in a real estate project without registering with Real Estate Regulatory Authority. Must maintain escrow account with 70% of funds. Must disclose project details, layout, approvals.

RERA Section 18 — Return of amount and compensation: If promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession, allottee shall be entitled to return of amount + interest (SBI MCLR + 2%) + compensation. If allottee wishes to stay, he is entitled to interest for delay.

Industrial Disputes Act Section 25F — Conditions precedent to retrenchment: No workman employed for 1 year+ in an industry shall be retrenched unless given one month's notice or pay in lieu, paid retrenchment compensation at 15 days' average pay per year of service, and notice served to appropriate government authority.

Maternity Benefit Act (amended 2017) Section 5 — Right to payment of maternity benefit: Maximum maternity benefit period: 26 weeks for first two children, 12 weeks for third child onwards. 12 weeks for adoptive/commissioning mothers. Paid at average daily wage. Creche facility mandatory for establishments with 50+ employees.

entries.source: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012
entries.text: POCSO Act Section 4 — Punishment for penetrative sexual assault: Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years, extendable to life, and fine. If victim below 16 years: minimum 20 years.

entries.source: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012
entries.text: POCSO Act Section 19 — Reporting of offences: Every person who has apprehension that an offence under this Act is likely to be committed or has knowledge that such an offence has been committed shall provide such information to Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police. Failure to report is an offence.

RTI Act Section 6 — Request for obtaining information: A person who desires to obtain information shall make a request in writing or through electronic means to the Public Information Officer specifying particulars of the information sought. Application fee Rs 10. No reasons required.

RTI Act Section 7 — Disposal of request: Public Information Officer shall, within 30 days from receipt of request, provide information or reject with reasons. 48 hours for life/liberty matters. First Appellate Authority within 30 days. Second appeal to Central/State Information Commission within 90 days.

Legal Services Authorities Act Section 12 — Criteria for giving legal services: Every person who is a member of SC/ST, victim of trafficking/disaster, woman, child, person with disability, industrial workman, person in custody, or person whose annual income does not exceed Rs 1 lakh shall be entitled to free legal services.

entries.source: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act 2013
entries.text: POSH Act Section 4 — Constitution of Internal Committee: Every employer with 10 or more employees shall constitute an Internal Committee. Presided over by a woman employed at a senior level, 2+ members from employees committed to women's causes, 1 external member from NGO/association committed to cause of women.

Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 — Framework for digital personal data protection. Data Fiduciary must obtain consent of Data Principal before processing personal data. Data Principal has right to access, correction, erasure of data. Data Fiduciary must notify data breach. Penalties up to Rs 250 crore for breach of obligations.

entries.source: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952
entries.text: EPF Act — Provident Fund contribution mandatory for establishments with 20+ employees. Employee contributes 12% of basic salary, employer contributes 12% (8.33% to EPS pension scheme, 3.67% to EPF). Interest rate fixed annually by government. Withdrawal allowed on retirement, death, or certain conditions.

Payment of Wages Act Section 15 — Claims arising out of deductions or delay in payment: Application before Payment of Wages Authority within 1 year of deduction/delay. Authority may direct payment of wages withheld + 10x compensation for malicious withholding.

BNSS Section 482 (replaces CrPC 438) — Anticipatory Bail: When any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, he may apply to Sessions Court or High Court for bail. Court considers: nature of accusation, antecedents, possibility of fleeing justice, danger of evidence being tampered.

BNSS Section 173 — Zero FIR: Every information relating to commission of a cognizable offence shall be recorded irrespective of the area in which the offence is committed. Such FIR (Zero FIR) shall be transferred to the police station having jurisdiction. This ensures no victim is turned away.

entries.source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
entries.text: Domestic Violence Act 2005 — Protects women in domestic relationships including marriage, live-in relationships, family. Remedies: Protection Orders, Residence Orders, Monetary Relief, Custody Orders, Compensation Orders. Supreme Court held live-in relationships covered under domestic relationship definition.

Guardians and Wards Act Section 17 — Welfare of minor paramount: Court in appointing guardian shall consider welfare of the minor as of paramount importance. Factors: age, sex, religion, character of guardian, wishes of deceased parent, existing custody. Mother generally preferred for children under 5.

NALSA (National Legal Services Authority) — Provides free legal aid to eligible persons. Toll-free number: 15100. Services: free legal consultation, court representation, mediation, Lok Adalat settlements. State Legal Services Authorities and District Legal Services Authorities operate at state and district level.

Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Amendment Act 2016 — Benami transaction: property held by person (benamidar) for the benefit of another (beneficial owner) who provides consideration. Punishment: 7 years rigorous imprisonment + fine up to 25% of fair market value. Property confiscated by government.

Limitation Act Section 65 — Adverse possession: Suit for possession of immovable property or any interest therein based on title by adverse possession: 12 years from when possession became adverse. Must be open, continuous, hostile, actual possession with intention to possess as owner.

Registration Act Section 17 — Documents of which registration is compulsory: Instruments of gift of immovable property, non-testamentary instruments purporting to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish rights in immovable property of value Rs 100 and above must be registered. Sale deed, mortgage deed, lease deed for over 1 year must be registered.

Industrial Disputes Act Section 11A — Powers of Labour Court/Tribunal to give appropriate relief: In an adjudication proceeding, Labour Court/Tribunal may set aside an order of dismissal or discharge and direct reinstatement with or without back wages, or award any other lesser punishment it deems just and equitable.

NGT Section 14 — Tribunal jurisdiction: National Green Tribunal shall have jurisdiction over all civil cases where a substantial question relating to environment including enforcement of legal rights relating to environment is involved. Covers air, water, soil pollution, forests, biodiversity, wetlands, hazardous substances.

BNSS Section 144 (replaces CrPC 125) — Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents: A Magistrate may order monthly allowance for maintenance of wife, legitimate/illegitimate minor children, and parents unable to maintain themselves. No income ceiling for wife's maintenance.

Power of Attorney — Authorises agent (attorney) to act on behalf of principal. General POA: broad authority for multiple transactions. Special POA: specific transaction only. Must be notarized. Registration required if related to immovable property transfer. POA ceases on death of principal.

BNSS Section 289 — Plea Bargaining: Available for offences with punishment up to 7 years (excluding offences against women/children and socio-economic offences). Accused files application admitting guilt. Court facilitates mutually satisfactory disposition. Minimum 1/4 prescribed punishment.

Article 20 — Protection in respect of conviction for offences: (1) No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of law in force at time of act. (2) No person shall be prosecuted and punished for same offence more than once (double jeopardy). (3) No person shall be compelled to be a witness against himself (right against self-incrimination).

Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) — Supreme Court expanded Article 21 to include right to live with dignity, right to livelihood. Held procedure must be just, fair and reasonable (not merely procedure prescribed by law). Established interconnection between Articles 14, 19, and 21 as golden triangle.

Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) — Supreme Court upheld constitutional validity of death penalty but restricted it to 'rarest of rare cases' doctrine. Court must consider aggravating and mitigating circumstances. Life imprisonment is rule; death is exception.

Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) — Supreme Court laid down Vishaka Guidelines for prevention of sexual harassment at workplace before POSH Act. Held sexual harassment violates Article 14, 15, 19, 21. Employer responsible for providing safe working environment. Led to POSH Act 2013.

Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017) — Supreme Court declared Triple Talaq (talaq-e-biddat) unconstitutional as it violates Article 14 and is manifestly arbitrary. Led to Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act 2019 criminalizing instant triple talaq.

Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) — Supreme Court (3-judge bench) held daughters have coparcenary rights in ancestral property under Hindu Succession Amendment Act 2005, even if father died before September 9, 2005. Daughters get equal rights as sons.

NALSA v. Union of India (2014) — Supreme Court recognized transgender persons as third gender and affirmed their fundamental rights under Articles 14, 15, 16, 19, 21. Directed government to take affirmative action for upliftment. Led to Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019.

Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) — Supreme Court propounded Basic Structure doctrine: Parliament cannot amend the Constitution to destroy its basic structure. Basic structure includes: supremacy of Constitution, republican and democratic form of government, separation of powers, federalism, secular character.

IT Act Section 67A — Punishment for publishing or transmitting of material containing sexually explicit act in electronic form: Punishable with imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh on first conviction. Up to 7 years on second conviction.

Hindu Marriage Act Section 13B — Divorce by mutual consent: Both parties to a marriage may present a petition for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent. Parties must have been separated for 1 year. Court grants decree after 6-18 months waiting period. Supreme Court can waive 6-month period in exceptional circumstances.

Industrial Disputes Act — Definitions: Award means an interim or final determination of any industrial dispute or any question relating thereto by any Labour Court/Tribunal. Settlement means written agreement between employer and workmen arrived at in course of conciliation proceeding. Retrenchment means termination of service of workman for any reason other than disciplinary action.
